messages.content: Tell me about the invitation for the reading.
Actually, never mind, tell me about the venue instead.

My lord, the reading will take place in the House’s Reading Hall, a modest chamber set within the northern wing of the Great Hall. The walls are faced in rough‑cut stone, their arches low to keep heat from the hearth at the centre. A long oak table sits in the middle, flanked by carved benches that face toward a single hearth where a fire crackles softly. Shelves of bound volumes line the far wall, but for this occasion only a single volume will be opened and read aloud. The room is dimmed by candles that sit in wrought‑iron holders, casting a steady glow across the pages. The quiet of the hall is kept by the thick stone walls, so voices are heard clear and without echo. The setting is simple but dignified; it provides a fitting backdrop for the words that will be read.
